question: Which French chemist was one of the first scientists to synthesise organic compounds such as formic acid, methane and acetylene from their elements?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Marcellin Berthelot.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thomsen-Berthelot principle** of thermochemistry was developed by** Republican politician** and **French chemist Marcellin Berthelot.**
 
• He created numerous **organic compounds** from inorganic compounds.
 
• He conducted studies on **reaction rates, the synthesis of hydrocarbons,** and **alcohols and carboxylic acids.**
 
• He researched **explosive mechanisms **and found several **compounds of coal tar.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Jacob Berzelius:**

 
 
• Jacob Berzelius is considered to be one of the** founders of modern chemistry.**
 
• He is referred to as the** "Father of Swedish Chemistry"** in Sweden.
 
• On **August 20th,** it is recognised as **Berzelius Day** in his honour.
 
 
 
• **Auguste Laurent:**
 
 
• French chemist Auguste Laurent contributed to the development of** organic chemistry **by discovering** Anthracene, Phthalic acid, and Carbolic acid.**
 
 
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier:**
 
 
• The** scientist and Nobleman Antoine Lavoisier were from France.**
 
• He challenged the** phlogiston idea** and recognised and called **oxygen (1778) and hydrogen (1783).**
